Magnesium reacts with sulfuric acid according to the following chemical equation: $Mg(s) + H_2SO_4(aq) \rightarrow MgSO_4(aq) + H_2(g)$
Line P on each graph shows how the volume of hydrogen formed changes with time when $1.2g$ of magnesium reacts with $40 \text{ cm}^3$ of $1.0 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ sulfuric acid at $20 \text{ °C}$.
($A_r$ value: $Mg = 24$)
Two further experiments were carried out and the volumes of hydrogen formed were plotted.
Experiment Q: $1.2g$ of magnesium + $40 \text{ cm}^3$ of $2.0 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ sulfuric acid at $20 \text{ °C}$
Experiment R: $1.2g$ of magnesium + $40 \text{ cm}^3$ of $0.5 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ sulfuric acid at $20 \text{ °C}$
Which lines show how the volume of hydrogen formed will change with time in each experiment?
